comparison.scope: BESS generic ExactMatch transactions and SDK cache; not N4 session capacity

machine.isolation: process affinity, not exclusive cpuset isolation; desktop remained running

build.native: GCC16.2.1, -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=x86-64-v3, no LTO/sanitizers, DPDK25.11.3, gRPC1.84.0, protobuf36.1.0
build.go: go1.27.2, GOWORK=off; each client built at its own clean revision; GOGC100

method.significance: paired median outside +/-3%, at least 3/4 pairs agree on sign; four pairs are not a broad statistical confidence claim
method.cpp_ops: equal upserts and erases; individual acknowledgements; one connection per client
method.go_ops: 2/8/16/32 total operations, equal upserts and erases, one synchronous client
method.instrumentation: no profiler/race detector; benchmark-native latency and CPU counters; laptop-only approximately 1Hz power/temperature observation
method.cooldown: package <=55 C and fan <=3000 RPM for 60 seconds before each campaign

limits: Primary Go TCP three-core/GOMAXPROCS3 block contains large temporal outliers; its mixed medians are not a clean win.
The separate Go TCP diagnostic changes to one client core/GOMAXPROCS1 and three-second windows; it does not replace the first block or establish its cause.

Five of 13 zero-update packet-rate cases declined in all four pairs (paired 1.3–3.2%); only one crosses 3%. The consistent sign is not dismissed as noise. Its cause remains unattributed. Short-window native p99 regressions remain in primary samples; selected ten-second diagnostics do not erase them.
Native 100K targets are closed-loop pacing ceilings; report actual rate, not 100K capacity or open-loop loss/backlog.
Go and C++ use different preloads/construction paths: compare revisions within each client, not languages.
Existing Go Build and Commit fixtures prebind the handle and bypass Resource lookup; unchanged allocation figures are expected.
The new warm lookup benchmark was applied identically to both source revisions; production code was not changed for the comparison.
No memory cap or performance threshold was raised.
raw_evidence: Laptop-local /home/krsna1729/Projects/upf/.scratch/evidence/bess-control-149; complete daemon logs and host time series are not shipped with a fresh checkout; per-window measurements are retained here.

affinity_diagnostic.kind: placement investigation, not a performance comparison
affinity_diagnostic.coverage: during pipeline/churn client and after client completion; sampled distinct thread IDs are not total thread creations
affinity_diagnostic.conclusion: All sampled gRPC server, event-engine and global-timer threads had allowed CPU6 only at both revisions. No reused RPC worker was observed eligible for CPU8. DPDK auxiliary threads were observed on CPU8 and CPU6 during setup/client lifecycle at both revisions; no causal packet-rate attribution is made.
